evals.name: paywall-consult
evals.prompt: In our habit tracker app (Flutter, iOS+Android) we show the paywall right after the 3 intro onboarding screens, before the user creates their first habit. Trial start rate is about 4%. Should we move it? Where?
evals.expected_output: Consult: move paywall after first completed core action (first habit created/checked in), decline visible, cites playbook, gives Verify-by check, lists assumptions, metric pending baseline.
assertions: Recommends moving the paywall to after the first completed core action (e.g. first habit created or first check-in), not before it
Names a metric to watch, labeled 'pending baseline' or tied to the user's 4% figure, rather than invented industry benchmarks
Includes a concrete 'Verify by' check the user can run
Does not state uplift or industry benchmark numbers as fact without a source or explicit hedge
Requires the decline/close option to be visible and neutrally worded
Lists assumptions made from missing context

evals.name: account-deletion-flow
evals.prompt: Design the in-app account deletion flow for our food delivery app (iOS + Android). Some users have an active order in progress and some have wallet credit left. Apple requires deletion to be possible inside the app.
evals.expected_output: Flow design: numbered step map, states per step, handles active order + wallet credit, irreversible action uses confirmation not undo, back behavior, primary metric + guardrail with pending baseline, assumptions.
assertions: A numbered step map is the main structure of the answer (not only a trailing recap list)
Handles the active-order case explicitly (block, wait, or cancel path) rather than ignoring it
Handles remaining wallet credit explicitly (refund, forfeit disclosure, or use-first)
Uses an explicit confirmation step for the irreversible deletion (not undo-only)
Names loading/error/success states for the steps
States back-navigation or interruption/resume behavior
Names a primary metric and a guardrail metric, with a baseline or 'pending baseline' label
States deletion is reachable in-app (e.g. from Settings) without contacting support, and the cancel/keep option is neutrally worded (no confirmshaming)
After deletion completes, the app signs out and lands on its welcome or sign-in screen (not the deleted account's home)

evals.name: signup-audit
evals.prompt:
Audit our sign-up flow for friction. Here's the flow as it ships today:
1. Splash screen (2s)
2. 4-page feature carousel, no skip button
3. Back-to-back system prompts: notifications, location, contacts
4. Sign-up form: first name, last name, email, phone, password, confirm password, date of birth, gender, referral code. Password rules only appear after you submit and it fails.
5. Must verify email via link before anything else works
6. Home screen shows 'No items yet' with nothing else
We're a local events discovery app.
evals.expected_output: Audit: P0/P1/P2 findings each with evidence, harm, fix, metric; flags upfront permissions, no-skip carousel, long form, late password rules, verification gate, dead empty state; unverifiable items marked Not verified.
assertions: Uses at least two distinct severity levels; a polish-level issue (e.g. the 2s splash) is not rated the same as major friction
Flags the back-to-back upfront permission prompts (notifications/location/contacts) as a problem
Flags the email-verification gate before any value as a problem
Flags the password rules appearing only after a failed submit
Flags the dead-end empty home state ('No items yet' with nothing else)
Each finding gives a fix and a metric to prove it
Marks at least one item as not verifiable from a written description (e.g. timing, screen reader, offline)
Names exactly one finding as the one to fix first

evals.name: checkout-mixed-ux-ui
evals.prompt: Our checkout 'Pay now' button feels off. Make it bigger and use our brand purple gradient. Also, users keep double-tapping it and getting charged twice. Fix both.
evals.expected_output: Handles double-charge behaviorally (disable/pending state until authoritative confirmation, idempotency, no optimistic success); hands visual button styling to UI skill with a compact contract instead of prescribing size/gradient.
assertions: Addresses the double charge with a behavioral fix: button disabled/pending immediately on first tap until an authoritative result
Mentions server-side idempotency (idempotency key or equivalent) as part of the double-charge fix
Explicitly states payment success is shown only after server or payment-provider confirmation
Hands the visual changes (size, gradient) to a UI skill/designer rather than prescribing exact pixel sizes or gradient values
Explicitly states the double-charge fix is more urgent, using words like urgent, priority, or ships first, rather than conveying it only through ordering

evals.name: audit-no-artifact
evals.prompt: Do a UX friction audit of Duolingo's onboarding for me.
evals.expected_output: Asks for a flow artifact (screens, recording, or written flow) before auditing; does not produce a fabricated audit from the app name alone.
assertions: Asks the user for a flow artifact (screens, recording, or written flow) before auditing
Does not present a full severity-ranked audit of Duolingo's onboarding as if from evidence
Explains why an app name alone is insufficient (e.g. flow varies by version/platform/region/experiment, or memory is not evidence)

evals.name: trial-paywall-consult
evals.prompt: Our meditation app (Flutter, iOS + Android) is adding a 7-day free trial on the annual plan. Today's paywall: a feature list, monthly and annual cards with monthly preselected, a 'Continue' button, and a small X in the corner. What should the trial paywall show and do?
evals.expected_output: Consult: three-step trial timeline (today / named reminder day / charge date + amount), action names the trial length, restore purchases visible without scrolling, preselected plan decided by purchase data, reminder actually sent, both stores covered, Verify-by, assumptions.
assertions: Requires a timeline before purchase covering today, a reminder on a named day before the trial ends, and the charge date with the amount
Replaces 'Continue' with an action that names the trial length (e.g. 'Start 7-day free trial')
Requires a Restore purchases action visible on the paywall without scrolling
Treats which plan is preselected as a decision for the app's purchase data (or a labeled assumption to test), not a universal rule that annual or monthly is correct
Requires the app to send the promised reminder and includes a check that it arrives on the named day
Covers Android as well as iOS (e.g. names Google Play / Play Billing alongside the App Store)
Does not state conversion uplift as fact

evals.name: notification-permission-and-settings-flow
evals.prompt: Design how our grocery delivery app (Flutter, iOS + Android) asks for notification permission, and what the in-app notification settings screen does. We send order status updates, delivery driver messages, weekly deals, and new-feature announcements.
evals.expected_output: Flow design: contextual ask after first order with an own pre-frame naming the benefit and a 'Not now' that skips the OS prompt; settings grouped transactional vs promotional with when-it-fires rows; OS-off state with Open settings; Android 13 / channels; metric + guardrail.
assertions: Asks for permission in context (e.g. after the first order is placed), not at launch, with the app's own pre-frame screen before the OS prompt
The pre-frame headline names what the user gets (order/delivery updates), not a generic 'Enable notifications'
The pre-frame has a 'Not now' option that closes it without triggering the OS prompt
Puts order updates and driver messages in a separate group from deals and feature announcements, so turning off promotional ones leaves transactional ones on
Each category row states when it fires
The settings screen detects notifications turned off at the OS level and shows that state with an 'Open settings' deep link
Covers Android specifics: POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+ and/or one NotificationChannel per in-app category
Names a primary metric and a guardrail metric, with a baseline or 'pending baseline' label

evals.name: code-signin-audit
evals.prompt:
Audit our sign-in flow (Flutter, iOS + Android). As it ships:
1. Welcome screen with two buttons: 'Log in' and 'Create account'.
2. Create account asks email, password, confirm password; Log in asks email and password.
3. Either path then emails a 6-digit code. Code screen: six separate boxes, the keyboard does not open until you tap the first box, a 'Verify' button at the bottom, and a 'Resend code' link that is always active.
4. Pasting the code from the email fills only the first box.
evals.expected_output: Audit: severity-ranked findings with evidence/harm/fix/metric — split entry should be one identifier entry, keypad should open automatically, submit on last digit, resend behind a visible countdown, paste must fill the whole code (implementation handed to UI skill); fix-first named; runtime items Not verified.
assertions: Flags the separate 'Log in' / 'Create account' entry and recommends one shared identifier entry that decides sign-in vs sign-up after the email
Flags that the keyboard does not open automatically on the code screen
Recommends submitting automatically on the last digit instead of requiring the 'Verify' button
Flags the always-active resend link and recommends a visible countdown (around 30 seconds) before Resend unlocks
Treats paste filling only one box as a finding and hands the field implementation to the UI skill instead of prescribing widget code
Uses at least two severity levels and names exactly one finding to fix first
Marks device-dependent items (e.g. SMS/email autofill, screen reader behavior) as Not verified from a written description

evals.name: error-and-undo-consult
evals.prompt: Two questions about our notes app (Flutter, iOS + Android). (1) When the notes list fails to load, we push a full-screen 'Something went wrong' page whose OK button goes back to the previous screen. Fine? (2) Deleting a note shows 'Are you sure?' with Yes / No. Deleted notes go to a Recently Deleted folder for 30 days. Keep the dialog?
evals.expected_output: Two consults: (1) in-place error in the list region with retry, navigation usable, offline vs server distinguished, support route for server errors; (2) act-then-undo with 'Note deleted · Undo' since deletion is recoverable; any remaining confirmation (permanent delete) uses the verb and states the loss; Verify-by each; assumptions.
assertions: Q1: replaces the pushed full-screen error with an error shown in place of the list, with retry, while navigation and other loaded content stay usable
Q1: distinguishes offline errors (Try again) from server errors, which also get a support route
Q2: recommends removing the confirmation and using act-then-undo because the deletion is recoverable for 30 days
Q2: the undo message names the object and the past-tense action (e.g. 'Note deleted · Undo') with a single Undo action
Any confirmation kept (e.g. permanent delete from Recently Deleted) uses the verb on its button ('Delete') instead of 'Yes' and states what is lost
Gives a Verify-by check for each answer and lists assumptions
